title: Design System: Ishan Mitra, The Rookie Set

display.purpose: The name on the pack wrapper; once per site.

nameplate.purpose: Client name on a card plate; container-scaled.

numeral.purpose: Every stat, serial, count and set code; tabular, kerning off because Advercase figure kerning is broken.

body.purpose: Prose; Helvetica Neue via local() only, never redistributed.

lead.purpose: Intro paragraph beside a section heading.

label.purpose: Nav, tabs, button text, chips; uppercase tracked bold.

shadows.name: panel-on-case
shadows.purpose: Stats and checklist stock panels; the pack wrapper uses -20px spread.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The single easing curve for every settle, lift and flip.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Arrow nudge, button lift, foil opacity.

motion.name: tilt-settle
motion.purpose: Card returning to rest; pointer tracking runs at 0.08s linear.

motion.name: flip
motion.purpose: Card flip to stat back; hero fan settle.

motion.name: stat-roll
motion.purpose: Numerals count up from zero via @property --n.

motion.name: deal
motion.purpose: Hero holos dealt in on load; no-preference only.

motion.name: tilt-range
motion.purpose: Pointer tilt; fine pointers without reduced motion only.

narrative.overview:
The site is a premium chrome sports-card set laid on a grading-case black ground. Every project is a 5:7 collectible card: the work fills the front inside a stock border, a nameplate carries the client and the role, and the flagships are holo parallels with a chrome frame and a refractor sheen that follows the pointer. Click a holo and it flips to a stock back with real stats that roll up from zero. Everything else on the page is made from the same parts as the card: pack wrapper, binder sheet and pockets, card-back stat tables, checklist cards, set codes ("IM·26"), and serials ("01/03").

The world is built from two materials, black case and bone card stock, and most surfaces are one or the other. Colour is rationed by role. Cobalt means booking a call, red marks flagship rarity, and the client work supplies every other colour. Type pairs a condensed, uppercase display face for nameplates and numerals with plain Helvetica Neue for prose, so the voice sits in the card furniture and the prose stays quiet. Desktop is bold: fanned holos, pointer tilt, the pack dealing itself in. Phones and reduced motion are calm: no tilt, a static sheen, a horizontal snap rail of cards.

The build supersedes the direction contract on type. The contract named Big Shoulders Display and Schibsted Grotesk, but the shipped faces are Advercase and Helvetica Neue.
keyCharacteristics: Two materials: grading-case black ground and bone card stock.
Every project is a 5:7 card with a 14px corner, a stock border and a nameplate.
Holo treatment (chrome frame, prizm refractor, red plate) appears only on flagships.
Numerals are display-face, tabular, with kerning off, and they roll in.
Colour is rationed by role, and the work supplies the rest of the palette.
Bold on desktop, calm on touch and under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Cobalt Means Book Rule
rules.body: Cobalt fills only a control that books the intro call. If clicking it does not lead to booking, it is not cobalt.

rules.name: The Rarity Red Rule
rules.body: Red marks a flagship holo and nothing else. It is not a hover colour, an emphasis colour or a decoration for non-flagship cards. On stock it is always red-ink.

rules.name: The Work Supplies Colour Rule
rules.body: Apart from the two signals, the only other colour on the page comes from the client work itself: card art, and swatch rows sampled from the work.

rules.name: The Kerning-Off Figures Rule
rules.body: Any figure set in Advercase uses the numeral role, with `font-kerning: none` and `'kern' 0`. The font's figure kerning is broken. Headings keep normal kerning.

rules.name: The No Redistribution Rule
rules.body: Helvetica Neue loads only through `local()`, and Helvetica or Arial is the fallback. Never self-host or bundle it; the licence does not allow it.

rules.name: The Printer's Voice Rule
rules.body: Advercase is always uppercase and always 700 in the shipped build. Prose is never set in it.

rules.name: The Objects Cast, Furniture Doesn't Rule
rules.body: Only physical things (cards, stock panels, the wrapper, devices) carry drop shadows. Tabs, buttons, nav and text never do.

rules.name: The Foil Is Earned Rule
rules.body: Chrome frame, prizm refractor and pointer glare at full strength belong to flagship holos only. Standard cards get only a faint glare.

dos: Do make every project a 5:7 card with a 14px corner, stock border, ink frame and a nameplate in the nameplate role.
Do set every stat, serial, count and set code in the numeral role (Advercase 700, tabular, kerning off).
Do keep cobalt for booking controls only, with white text and the cobalt-hi hover.
Do use red-ink, never red, when red text sits on card stock.
Do turn off tilt on coarse pointers and under reduced motion, and leave the sheen as a static gradient.
Do use inline stroked SVG for icons and arrows.
Do keep Helvetica Neue on `local()` with the Helvetica and Arial fallback.
donts: Don't use cobalt for anything that doesn't book a call.
Don't use red on non-flagship cards, as a hover colour or as general emphasis.
Don't give standard cards the chrome frame, prizm foil or red plate. Holo is a rarity.
Don't self-host or ship Helvetica Neue files.
Don't turn on kerning for Advercase figures.
Don't put drop shadows on buttons, tabs, nav or text.
Don't add tiny uppercase labels above headings. Set codes and serials belong on cards, chips and stat panels, not as section kickers.
